incidents.vector: Exploited a zero-day authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-123890) in VMware vCenter's Directory Service, chained with an earlier BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, to forge administrator sessions.
incidents.impact: The group (tracked as Armory Castle, formerly UNC5221) gained full control of victims' vSphere environments, exfiltrating credential databases and deploying custom malware for persistence; the flaw is now being actively exploited in the wild and Broadcom has released patches.

incidents.victim: Universities in East Asia (two institutions, unnamed)
incidents.vector: Attackers running the autonomous AI penetration-testing framework Cairn discovered and exploited a previously unknown path-traversal zero-day in an open-source medical imaging AI application to obtain shell access.
incidents.impact: Amazon's threat intelligence team observed the AI agents breach two university servers using the zero-day with minimal human direction; the vulnerability has since been patched and affected organizations notified via a government partner.

incidents.victim: Financial services, healthcare, and legal organizations (multiple, unnamed; US, UK, Australia)
incidents.vector: Com-affiliated actors, including Bling Libra (ShinyHunters) and newly tracked clusters Vortex and Cinder, used vishing calls impersonating IT support to steer employees to adversary-in-the-middle phishing pages that captured credentials and MFA approvals.
incidents.impact: Attackers exfiltrated data from Microsoft 365, SharePoint, and OneDrive at targeted organizations and sent extortion demands via internal Teams and email, threatening to publish stolen client and patient data.

incidents.victim: 40+ Irish and UK credit unions (via software supplier Wellington IT)
incidents.vector: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in systems operated by Belfast-based software supplier Wellington IT, which provides mobile banking apps used by credit unions.
incidents.impact: Payment details belonging to members who used the affected mobile banking apps were accessed; the vulnerability was patched October 6 but affected credit unions were not notified until November 16, a six-week delay regulators called unacceptable.

incidents.vector: The n0n data-extortion group, which has used AI coding agents to write and scale its attack tooling, breached systems at The Container Store.
incidents.impact: The attack forced the retailer to take down online ordering and resort to alternative in-store transaction processing for about a week; the company found no evidence customer financial data was stolen, though the group has listed it on its leak site.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack at the end of October, reportedly involving the ARTEX AI penetration-testing tool, took down the European Commission's internal Sysper HR platform.
incidents.impact: EU staff have been unable to access the system used for timesheets, payroll, training sign-ups, and leave requests for nearly a month.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed a test environment at Rakuten's securities division and extracted customer account records.
incidents.impact: Data on more than 15 million customer accounts was stolen, including sensitive information for roughly 4.4 million accounts; the company says passwords, PINs, and other authentication data were not exposed.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack of undetermined origin struck the West Virginia Legislature's IT systems, prompting officials to disable access to certain systems while investigating.
incidents.impact: The attack took down the Legislature's website and disrupted internal IT systems for multiple days; no group has claimed responsibility and officials have not confirmed whether ransomware was involved.

incidents.vector: Attackers ran a brute-force credential attack against Germany's BundID digital-identity portal over a weekend.
incidents.impact: At least 10,000 user accounts were compromised; officials locked the affected accounts and are notifying owners.

incidents.vector: Norwegian energy company Equinor disclosed a cybersecurity breach affecting part of its IT environment.
incidents.impact: The company says the incident has not affected production capabilities; further details on scope and attacker access have not been disclosed.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached Ethiopian Airlines' ShebaMiles frequent-flyer loyalty platform.
incidents.impact: Customer data associated with loyalty program accounts was stolen; the airline has not disclosed the full scope of affected records.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached cloud infrastructure at cybersecurity and IT provider N-able, accessing its Mail Assure and SpamExperts servers.
incidents.impact: N-able says it found no evidence that customer data was stolen and is rebuilding the affected services; given N-able's role serving managed service providers, a deeper compromise could have had downstream supply-chain effects.

incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a data analysis tool to access CodinGame's internal network and copy data from its databases.
incidents.impact: Stolen data includes user details and platform activity history; the company has notified affected members.

incidents.victim: Mr. Cooper (Nationstar Mortgage) and Rocket Mortgage
incidents.vector: Threat actors impersonated Mr. Cooper employees in phone calls to the company's IT help desk to fraudulently obtain temporary passwords, bypassing multi-factor authentication to access internal systems.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole large amounts of private customer data in a 2023 breach; New York's Department of Financial Services fined Rocket Mortgage (which later acquired Mr. Cooper) $2 million and Mr. Cooper $4.75 million for MFA failures, delayed incident reporting, and inadequate risk assessments.

incidents.vector: An attacker used a cloud access key Barracuda had issued to a third-party AI service provider and failed to revoke, gaining entry to Barracuda's cloud environment.
incidents.impact: The intruder deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access across Barracuda's internal network and other cloud environments over roughly two days before being detected and evicted.

incidents.vector: A newly identified group dubbed SilentAir compromises telecom infrastructure and plants backdoors that issue malicious SS7 and Diameter signaling commands.
incidents.impact: The group can track subscriber locations, collect device data, and intercept calls and SMS traffic for selected targets; the activity has been ongoing since early 2025.

incidents.victim: EU politicians and law enforcement officials (18 individuals, including Eurojust and Europol leadership)
incidents.vector: The pro-Kremlin hacktivist group NoName057(16) compiled and published personal information (doxing) on high-profile European officials and journalists.
incidents.impact: Victims included Italy's Foreign Minister, the Eurojust president, Europol's cybercrime unit chief, Germany's federal police president, and journalists who have investigated Russian influence operations, raising personal-safety and intimidation concerns.

incidents.victim: 178 organizations using Optimizely, including BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger, and Zoom
incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation A/B-testing platform to inject malicious JavaScript directly into customer accounts, served from Optimizely's trusted CDN.
incidents.impact: Visitors to at least 178 websites were served code that swapped cryptocurrency addresses, skimmed payment card data, and attempted zero-click exploit delivery against older iPhones and iPads; Optimizely patched the flaw and removed the injected code within a day.

incidents.victim: French supermarkets and food retailers (approximately 700 stores)
incidents.vector: French officials attributed the attack to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh military cyber unit, which compromised commercial refrigeration control systems.
incidents.impact: The hack disrupted refrigeration at roughly 700 retail locations including supermarkets, butchers, food factories, and a slaughterhouse, causing tens of millions of euros in losses.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor, defense, and civil-society organizations (19 targeted, 10 compromised; unnamed)
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers paired the open-source Cairn AI penetration-testing framework with domestic AI models (Zhipu GLM, DeepSeek) to autonomously plan and execute 25 intrusion operations against 19 organizations.
incidents.impact: Confirmed unauthorized access or data theft at 10 organizations, including exposure of over one million records at a US teachers' union, creation of rogue admin accounts at a semiconductor manufacturer, and tampering with a live industry standards-ballot document.
